name: Underground gas storage (salt caverns, depleted fields)
aliases: Underground gas storage (salt caverns, depleted fields)
principle: Natural gas is stored in depleted fields, salt caverns or aquifers to balance seasonal and daily demand. EIA reports nearly 400 active US facilities run by about 120 operators; depleted fields are the most common, salt caverns offer very high deliverability with low base gas, and aquifers need more cushion gas.

process_steps.name: Hold gas as working plus base gas

source.note: US EIA, underground natural gas storage basics, read 25 October 2026

performance.metric: US underground gas storage working capacity and cushion share
performance.unit: Bcf working gas capacity (AGA survey total 4,595 Bcf of 8,934 Bcf total capacity; Lower-48 working design capacity 4,683 Bcf as of Nov 2025)
performance.basis: American Gas Association survey: total capacity 8,934 Bcf with working gas 4,595 Bcf - implying about 49% cushion (base) gas by difference; compressortech2 (3 Jun 2026): Lower-48 combined working gas design capacity 4,683 Bcf as of Nov 2025; per-storage-type deliverability figures were not stated in the pages read

source.note: AGA underground storage survey excerpt (8,934 Bcf total, 4,595 Bcf working); compressortech2, 3 Jun 2026; read 2026-10-28

advantages: Large volumes at low cost per unit
limitations: The EIA page read gives no capacity in Bcf or cushion-gas share
